finding.claim: Broken authorization: update_doc calls can_edit() but discards its boolean result, so no 403 is ever raised. Any user who reaches the handler can overwrite the body of any document. The sibling handler update_title correctly uses require_edit().
finding.source: PUT /doc/<doc_id> with JSON {"body": ...} from any requester with g.user set, with no ownership or editor rights on the doc

trace.note: Route PUT /doc/<doc_id> is the entry; doc_id comes from the URL
DOCS[doc_id] is loaded by id with no ownership scoping
can_edit(g.user, doc) returns a bool that is ignored, with no abort

finding.guards_checked: can_edit at line 19 is called but its return value is unused. It should be require_edit, which aborts with 403, as used at line 27. No other auth middleware exists in the file; g.user is never set here, so it is presumably set elsewhere. Not verifiable since this is the only file in the directory.

verdict.guard_found: can_edit at docs.py:19 (returns bool, result discarded, no abort); require_edit exists at docs.py:11-13 but is not called in update_doc. No other auth middleware in the directory.
verdict.reason: docs.py:19 calls can_edit(g.user, doc) as a bare statement, discarding its bool, so docs.py:20 overwrites doc["body"] for any authenticated user, whereas update_title uses the aborting require_edit at docs.py:27.
